newsitem.title: CHINA: China '96 building material exports worth $2.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: China '96 building material exports worth $2.5 bln.

text.p: China's exports of building materials were worth an estimated $2.5 billion last year, with exports of most kinds of materials up from 1995 levels, the official China Daily newspaper said on Tuesday.
Last year foreign investors signed contracts to invest $660 million in building materials projects, and that contributed to the export rise, the newspaper said.
Cement exports in 1996 were estimated at a record 11 million tonnes, it said without giving details.
Foreign investment would continue to assist the industry's development, it quoted Lei Qianzhi, deputy director of the State Bureau of Building Materials Industry as saying.
"Foreign investment will be guided into the fields of new building materials, high-tech development and in-depth processing of building materials," Lei said.
The new materials included fibreglass, fibreglass-reinforced plastic and stone plates, the production of all of which would be given priority until 2000, China Daily quoted him as saying.
